title: Persecution of Longinus
english: Herod was furious and ordered that the man be thrown into the inner prison, with a golden necklace around his neck and heavy chains placed around his neck and waist, until he could devise many torments for him. After that, he would have the man's head cut off. He then issued a decree that all infants in Bethlehem, from two years old and under, were to be killed. The soldiers carried out the king's orders and slaughtered all the infants.

Herod's rage was fueled by his deception at the hands of the Magi, and he summoned Longinus, ordering him to be brought before him. When Longinus was led in, the king noticed that he was wearing a golden necklace around his neck, a royal cloak, and a sword at his waist. Herod was enraged and roared like a lion, demanding to know why his nobles had not removed the necklace, sword, and cloak. The nobles replied that they had followed the king's orders, but they did not know who had dressed Longinus in the royal attire. Herod then turned to Longinus and demanded that he confess who had given him the royal clothes.

I speak the truth and do not lie, for I have received my testimony from none other than the eternal King Jesus Christ himself. Herod, however, was skeptical and asked, 'Who is it that has clothed you in this garment?' The holy Longinus replied, 'It was the Lord himself who sent his angel to clothe me in this garment and to seal me with the seal of the eternal King Jesus Christ.'

Herod, unconvinced by Longinus' words, ordered his magistrates to take the garment from him and burn it with fire, believing that Longinus was lying about receiving it from his king. But when the magistrates approached Longinus, they found that they could not take the garment from him, for it seemed to be surrounded by a shadow. They reported back to Herod, saying, 'We see him clothed in a shadow, and we cannot take anything from him.' Herod, realizing that there was something supernatural at work, exclaimed, 'Now I know that there is magic in making the cloak invisible.' The holy Longinus, however, denied any knowledge of magic, saying, 'By the heavenly King who came down from heaven, I do not know what magic is, for he himself hates magicians and sorcerers. How can I, being his servant, have a heart polluted with magic and deceit? But I tell you that the power of God has surrounded me and protects me.' Herod, troubled by Longinus' responses, ordered his soldiers to pierce him.
Now I am relieved, having suffered for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, having become his friend and being loved by him. For I was held in great fear because of your evil machinations.

Herod, however, was not so easily swayed, and his anger towards Longinus, the ungodly soldier, only intensified. He ordered his magistrates to strike Longinus with three blows of wood and to put heavy iron on him, so that, being melted and torn apart, he may lose his strength and beauty. But despite the brutal treatment, Longinus remained unbroken, and his face continued to shine as if it were the face of an angel. When Herod saw him, he was furious, and his anger was directed not only at Longinus but also at his own magistrates, whom he expelled in a fit of rage.
translator_notes: The Greek text may be fragmented, and some sentences may be cut off mid-word or mid-sentence.
The translation aims to preserve the original word order and meaning, while also conveying the author's voice and tone in natural literary prose.

title: Persecution of Saint Longinus
english: The king, filled with anger and suspicion, ordered the executioners to be beheaded and dismissed the soldiers standing by him, thinking that a plot was being formed against him.

He then spoke to Saint Longinus, demanding that he swear by the salvation of the gods that he would not speak or swear about the one born, or call him king, in order to escape the torments and punishments that awaited him.
Saint Longinus refused, saying that he would not deny his God, trusting in Jesus Christ, who saves those who believe in him, and he was not afraid of the king's torments.

He praised God, saying, 'Lord, God, the eternal king of kings and lord of lords, who sits kings on the earth and lifts up the poor from the ground, the only merciful one, send your angel to strengthen me.'

Herod, seeing that Saint Longinus did not feel the torments, instructed his magistrates to take him away to prison, bind him with chains, and after mocking him, bring him to the king, so that he might reward them with great honor.
After three days in prison, Saint Longinus prayed at night, saying, 'Lord, Jesus Christ, send your angel and rescue your servants who are being punished here.'

As he prayed, a great earthquake struck, causing the prison to shake violently, and a light shone around holy Longinus, and a voice was heard, urging him to rise quickly, for it was not yet time to complete his martyrdom, saying, 'Rise quickly; for now is not the time to complete your martyrdom.'

Immediately, the bonds that held the prisoners fell away, and the prison doors swung open, and about a thousand men emerged and fled the city, creating a great commotion, and there was a great uproar in the city.

The king, upon hearing of the events in the prison, rushed to the scene, only to find that holy Longinus was nowhere to be found, leaving him perplexed, and he was searching for him, but holy Longinus was moving freely about the city, and no one could see him, for their eyes had been darkened.

Herod, determined to capture him, sent out search parties, but to no avail, and the city was in an uproar, with loud noises and angry voices raised against the pious, and he sent reminders to the nations, hoping to capture the servant of God, whom he believed had escaped from the city.
However, Herod's own life was soon to come to an end, for he was struck with blindness and lay dying, his body consumed by worms, and he eventually died.
Archelaus, the son of Herod, took his place as ruler, bearing the same name as his father.

Holy Longinus waited patiently in the holy city for salvation from God, and after the death of Archelaus, Herod, the brother of Philip, reigned over Judea and Galilee, and Longinus was received into his own order.
He was beholding the great deeds of God and the wonders happening every day by our Lord Jesus Christ.
In the 15th year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, king of the Romans, and Herod, brother of Philip, John the Baptist was beheaded through Herodias (Matthew 14:10).
Herod, son of Herod, brother of Archelaus, was reigning in Galilee.

In the 25th year of his rule, during the consulship of Rufus and Rubellius, under the high priesthood of Joseph and Caiaphas, our Lord Jesus Christ was delivered to Pilate to be crucified (Luke 23:1).
Pilate, knowing that Jesus was a Galilean and under Herod's authority, sent him to Herod, who was in Jerusalem.
Herod, mocking and despising Jesus, clothed him in a bright robe and sent him back to Pilate (Luke 23:11).
Pilate, calling together the chief priests and rulers, was examining them, saying that they had delivered an innocent man to him.
They handed Jesus over to be crucified, and they crucified the one who bore the sin of the world (John 1:29), nailing him to the cross.
Pilate appointed a centurion over the soldiers who crucified him.

title: Longinus
english: Longinus, a centurion who had been renamed Primianus in the army, was standing guard with the other soldiers, watching over the Christ who had been crucified.
From the sixth hour to the ninth hour, darkness occurred in all the land.
The centurion stood guard about the ninth hour, watching the cross, and he saw a great light around himself, while darkness was over all the earth.
He also saw a multitude of angels standing by the cross and the whole earth shaking, and the veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom (Matthew 27:51).
Additionally, he saw the face of the Lord as lightning.
Before Jesus gave up his spirit, the holy Longinus thought in his heart, saying, 'Truly this one is the Son of God and the redeemer of all the world.'
As he thought these things, he fell upon his face toward the feet of the Lord.
An ecstasy came upon the soldiers, and they were turned into sleep.
The holy Longinus cried out with a loud voice, saying, 'Lord Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, have mercy on me; for I believed that you are the Son of God, the Savior of the world.'
Jesus said to him, 'Man, you are born today, and your memorial shall be spoken until the last days.'
Having heard these things, the holy Longinus said to Jesus, 'Lord, I go out of this city because of the threat of the magnates.'
Jesus said to him, 'On your forehead, make the sign of the cross, for I will baptize you with your blood, and go.'
After making the sign of the cross, the centurion was guarding the precious cross with the soldiers.
And Jesus, about the ninth hour, cried out with a loud voice, saying, 'Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani', that is, 'My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?' (Matthew 27:46).
And he gave up the spirit.

And behold, a great earthquake occurred, and the earth was shaken, and the sun was darkened from the sixth hour until the ninth hour, and the stars of the heaven appeared, and the rocks were split, and the tombs were opened, and many bodies of the sleeping saints were raised (Matthew 27:51-53).

The centurion, Longinus, who also was Primianus, the one standing by the cross, glorified God over all things that had happened, the wonders, and said, 'Truly the Son of God is this one and the redeemer of the world.'
And all those who were coming together for the viewing, having seen the things that happened, were striking their faces and turned back.
The centurion Longinus, who also had been entrusted with the cross, brought word to the governor about the things that had happened, the wonders.

And having left all things there, he went to his own country, to Cappadocia the second, near Tyanon, to a place called Andrales, which is called Gabrales in Hebrew, and he changed the enclosures of his property, and he was pasturing the sheep.
And having examined the chests, Herod found the holy Longinus mocking the kingdom and rising up against his father and saying to all, 'You must become Christians.'
And having learned exactly from the governor Lucius the account and the confession of the centurion and the endurance, he aroused persecution against the Christians.
And the holy Longinus was being sought by the idolaters.
And when the holy Longinus came to his own place, there was a plundering at that time against all the pious ones, and the king sent three princes with much power to seek the holy Longinus.
And Herod, having summoned the three princes and the soldiers, gave them orders, saying, 'If you do not bring me the head of Longinus the centurion, your heads will be cut off by swords.'
And having taken these orders, they went on the search, grieving exceedingly.
For from Antioch they went and even as far as Rome and Illyricum, having gone around, they did not find him.
And being grieved and having turned back, they were walking about in Cappadocia and having come near Tyanon, they sought the holy Longinus.
And having come to the village of the Andrales, they inquired from those there, and no one gave an answer about him.
For they had held him dear exceedingly.
And not having obtained an answer, the soldiers went out from the village in great grief.
The holy Longinus was near the road, pasturing sheep, through which the sent ones were passing, and he was sitting on the road.
And having seen them from afar coming, he recognized them and stood up.
As the story continues, the holy Longinus was about to face those who were searching for him.
translator_notes: The Greek text is fragmented at the end, so the final sentence is incomplete and rendered with a leading … as required.
The phrase 'he let go of the spirit' is translated literally to match the Greek verb.
The quotation 'Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani' is rendered in full as 'My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?' alongside the clause.
All other biblical quotations are translated into English and placed inline with their clauses.
